steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The two main Islamic festivals are Id-ul-Adha (Festival of Sacrifice) and Id-ul-Fitr (Festival of Fast-Breaking). Shi'a Muslims also observe Ashura , commemorating the martyrdom of Imam Husayn.

steps.title: RS Exam Tips — Islamic Festivals
steps.body: 1. For Islamic Festivals questions, always include specific scriptural or source references where relevant 2. Explain both religious and non-religious viewpoints 3. Use specialist vocabulary precisely (e.g. terms from the specification) 4. Evaluate by analysing strengths and weaknesses of different views before reaching your conclusion 5. Link your discussion of Islamic Festivals to its real-world impact on believers and society

steps.title: UK Context
steps.body: In 2023, the East London Mosque hosted over 10,000 worshippers for Id-ul-Fitr prayers, with additional prayer spaces set up in local parks. The mosque also distributed 2,000 free meals to the local community, regardless of faith, as part of the Id celebration.

steps.title: UK Context
steps.body: Islamic Relief UK’s qurbani programme distributes meat to over 2 million people in 30 countries each year. British Muslims can pay for qurbani online, specifying where the sacrifice should take place, with many choosing to have it performed in conflict zones or areas affected by famine where the need is greatest.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always refer to specific sources of authority (scripture, sacred texts, religious leaders) Explain contrasting beliefs — different views within and between traditions Use key terminology precisely (e.g. tawhid, atonement, sanctity of life) For 12-mark evaluation questions, consider both sides before reaching a justified conclusion Link beliefs to their impact on individuals, communities and society Acknowledge diversity — no religious tradition has a single, uniform view
